page: Microsoft Azure F32als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB, resulting in a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 32 MB of L3 cache, full support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, and hardware-level cryptographic acceleration including AES and SHA-NI.

The F32als_v7 does not bundle local ephemeral storage and does not include a GPU. Storage needs are met exclusively through remote Azure Premium Storage attachments. This profile maintains resource cost efficiency by avoiding the hardware overhead of unused local solid-state drives or accelerators, dedicating server capacity strictly to processing tasks.

Performance testing reflects strong compute throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution and single-threaded data compression, reaching 41.01 GB/sec in gzip benchmarks. Multi-threaded CPU performance ranks in the top 25 percent across stress-ng and PassMark CPU suites. Leveraging AVX-512 instructions, the server delivers top-tier prompt processing on small language models, achieving 4,734.1 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models, though inference capacity drops to average percentiles on 70B models due to the 64.0 GB memory ceiling.

The hardware configuration targets compute-bound workloads where memory density is a secondary requirement. Typical use cases include data compression pipelines, build automation, CPU-based small-model inference, static web delivery, and distributed batch processing.
